A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DASH and contain readable methods, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Full text and visual inspection support reliable matching across versions, including the added Appendix F.

before.justification: v2 reports original DASH experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet, including attack comparisons, transferability, ablations, and appendix black-box results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and reports revised black-box results with uncertainty estimates and additional architectural transfer results.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, softmax-weighted attack composition, stage chaining, meta-loss, and base-attack pool remain unchanged. Combining query-based attacks was already documented in v2 Appendix D; v3's expanded explanations do not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same datasets, image-classification task, and white-box, transfer-based, query-based, and post-processing settings. Adding XCiT-M12 changes the evaluated model architecture within existing coverage; the five disjoint image subsets change sampling, not dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The attack comparators in Tables 1, 2, and 5 are retained. New Table 8 extends the same transfer-comparison methods—PI-FGSM++, CW, AutoAttack, DiffAttack, and AdvAD—to another source/target model without adding an attack baseline.

E3.justification: Table 2 now averages only off-diagonal transfer results, excluding same-model attacks. Table 8 adds XCiT-M12 as a surrogate and target. Appendix D reports evaluation over five disjoint 1,000-image subsets, whereas v2 states 1,000-image sampling without this additional design. Core benchmark settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix F and Table 8 extend the transferability analysis to explicitly test transfer between Wide-ResNets and a transformer. Existing analyses of learned weights, stage count, attack-pool composition, perceptual loss, and weight transfer are retained.

E5.justification: Table 5 newly reports means and standard deviations across five disjoint 1,000-image sets, replacing point estimates. These quantify variation across sampled sets, not an established increase in training seeds. Both versions retain the 100 repetitions of the random-weight ablation.

E6.justification: Table 2's revised averaging changes Addepalli-surrogate DASH ASR from 75.27 to 63.30, below AdvAD's 64.70, while pairwise scores remain unchanged. Table 5 replaces point estimates with five-subset summaries; ViT DASH/Sign Hunter averages become 71.11/70.96 versus 70.22/69.24 previously. Table 8 adds XCiT results. Figure 3 corrects random/trained average ASR from 78.26/96.57 to 78.18/99.77. Tables 1, 3, 4, 6, and 7 retain their numerical results.

T1.justification: The attack equations, objectives, and perceptual-metric formulas are mathematically unchanged. Clarified classifier notation and the new conceptual discussion of convex-hull search introduce no formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution bullet drop the explicit claim that the meta-loss is novel, modestly narrowing the stated novelty. The central claims about differentiable multi-stage composition, attack effectiveness, perceptual quality, and generalization remain.

C2.justification: Sections 3–4 add interpretations involving continuous interpolation, the convex hull of attack trajectories, and optimization in a low-dimensional weight space. Section 5.3 describes Addepalli transfer performance as similar to AdvAD rather than superior, and Appendix F discusses architectural generalization. Existing CW-gradient explanations and distortion tradeoffs remain.

D1.justification: v2 says code accompanies the supplementary material; v3 supplies a specific repository address in the abstract. v3 also clarifies baseline hyperparameter tuning versus fixed DASH base-attack settings and identifies the black-box ViT as base-sized. Core implementation, hardware, and training details are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Debenedetti et al.'s robust-vision-transformer work for the XCiT evaluation and sharpens the contrast with prior attack ensembles as discrete selection versus continuous interpolation. Other reference changes largely update metadata or consolidate duplicate citations to the same works.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites and clarifications in the abstract, threat model, related work, results, and conclusion, plus corrected terminology and typos. v3 adds an acknowledgment and Appendix F and shortens affiliation text, while preserving the main narrative and section order.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 8 and reformats Table 5 for mean-plus-standard-deviation entries using substantially smaller type. Several tables are more compact, Figure 3's rendering and caption change, and content reflows. The other principal figures retain their content and design.

improvement.justification: Corrected transfer averages and Figure 3 means improve numerical accuracy, while uncertainty reporting and the architectural transfer test strengthen empirical support. These are limited gains: the core method and main benchmark remain unchanged, Table 5 becomes harder to read, and prose still overstates uniform transfer superiority and a roughly one-point ViT black-box advantage where Table 5 shows only 0.15 points.
